core_claim.quote: The prefrontal cortex is posited to play a key role in the GNW because of the greater density of neurons thought to be critical for global broadcasting of information, but it is not proposed as the exclusive territory for conscious access.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: What is consciously seen is represented in prefrontal cortex, so that its content can be decoded there, whether or not the person has to report it or use it in a task.

first_stated.passage: Global information sharing and routing would rely on a set of interconnected high-level cortical regions forming a ‘global workspace’ and involving primarily the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, but also additional hubs in inferior parietal cortex, mid-temporal cortex, and precuneus

source.citation: Dehaene S, Charles L, King J-R, Marti S. Toward a computational theory of conscious processing. Current Opinion in Neurobiology 25:76-84, 2014

prediction.test_for: Features of a stimulus that the person consciously sees (its category, orientation, identity) can be decoded from prefrontal activity, including when the stimulus or the feature is irrelevant to the task and nothing is reported.
prediction.test_against: A feature the person consciously sees can be decoded from sensory cortex but not from prefrontal cortex, in a design sensitive enough to find it in prefrontal cortex for other features.

study.name: The Cogitate Consortium's adversarial test of global workspace and integrated information theory

source.citation: Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642:133-142, 2025

data_collected.basis: The registration was created on OSF on 2019-01-16, and the protocol says the original and amended registrations were frozen before data acquisition began.

passages.text: On the basis of our preregistered predictions and pre-approved interpretations27 (Extended Data Table 1), the theories would pass the test if decoding is possible for both category (in at least one category pairing) and orientation (in at least one category), but would fail otherwise.

source.citation: Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642:133-142, 2025

passages.text: Hence, across modalities, face–object decoding occurred in both posterior and prefrontal ROIs, consistent with IIT and GNWT predictions.

source.citation: Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642:133-142, 2025

passages.text: We obtained divergent results for IIT and GNWT: decoding of face orientation (left, right or front views) was achieved in posterior but not in prefrontal ROIs, both with iEEG (Fig. 2f,h, approximately 95% with pseudotrial aggregation; Extended Data Fig. 3a) and the fMRI searchlight approach (Fig. 2g, approximately 45%). Decoding of face orientation was robust from MEG cortical time series in posterior ROIs (approximately 75% with pseudotrial aggregation), but was weaker, yet above chance (35%), in prefrontal ROIs (Fig. 2i), with a possibility of signal leakage from posterior regions (Extended Data Fig. 3b).

source.citation: Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642:133-142, 2025
